Hi Daniel — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below and I attached a compact roster (support_roster_oct2028.pdf) for quick review. If you want, we can convert the roster into your template.

1) Technical Account coverage ("coverage lattice"):
- Primary TAM: assigned Monday–Friday 08:30–17:30 local (customer timezone), overlap window with engineering 09:30–11:30 for handoffs.
- Secondary/backfill TAM: available weekdays 08:30–17:30 and acts as primary during scheduled PTO / handoffs.
- Global on-call engineer: 24x7 for Sev1 escalation (rotating weekly).

2) Escalation paths:
- Tier 1: TAM triage (first response within 60 minutes for Sev1, 4 hours for Sev2 during business hours).
- Tier 2: On-call engineering (page within 30 minutes of TAM triage confirmation for Sev1).
- Tier 3: Engineering lead + SRE (escalate within 2 hours for unresolved Sev1).
- All Sev1 incidents trigger an immediate incident bridge and executive notification per your stakeholder list.

3) Weekend & holiday coverage:
- Weekend coverage performed by on-call engineering; TAM rotates weekly and is paged for confirmed Sev1 incidents only.
- Primary TAM is not paged for informational alerts on weekends unless incident severity meets Sev1 criteria.

4) Incident communications:
- Initial Acknowledgement: within SLO windows above.
- Incident Bridge: created within 30 minutes of Sev1 confirmation.
- Stakeholder updates: every 60 minutes until resolution for Sev1; ad-hoc for Sev2 based on impact.
- Post-incident report: delivered within 3 business days.

5) Evidence & retention:
- We retain audit logs (control plane and request logs) for 1 year by default; extended retention can be contracted.

Attachments: support_roster_oct2028.pdf (application/pdf - stub)

If you need the incident notification matrix and the detailed on-call policy document, Marissa can attach those — I flagged this as high priority. Happy to jump on a 30-min call to walk through the lattice if helpful.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova

Redwood Inference
